_README: Copy this file to add an application -- one joint on one robot. Put it in
applications/ (gitignored) rather than in here, which is public.
cp applications/examples/_TEMPLATE.json applications/my_elbow.json
./eval_actuator.py -a robstride_00 -j my_elbow --save --charts
Delete any field you do not need. Requirements you leave out are derived
from the motion profile instead. Do NOT invent numbers to fill gaps: an
omitted field gets a documented default and shows up in the report's
assumption list and sensitivity sweep, whereas a fabricated one looks like
data and silently corrupts the verdict.
UNITS. Every physical value may be written three ways:
1. explicit object   "com_distance": {"value": 11, "units": "in"}  <- preferred
2. suffixed name     "com_distance_mm": 280
3. bare number       "com_distance": 0.28   -> canonical SI assumed, and
flagged with ! in the report's UNIT AUDIT
A unit from the wrong dimension (kg for a length) is always a hard error.
Set "strict_units": true to reject form 3 outright.
Canonical units: mass kg, length m, inertia kg.m^2, angle rad, time s,
torque N.m, angular velocity rad/s, temperature degC, voltage V.
MINIMUM VIABLE ENTRY: a name, a load, and either a profile or duty_segments.
Everything else has a defensible default.
name: My Elbow
_n_actuators: How many actuators share this joint in parallel. Torque and mass scale by n
and each unit carries 1/n of the load, so every unit's thermal problem gets
easier. Compare options with -n 1,2,3 on the command line rather than
_ratio: Extra reduction between the actuator OUTPUT and the joint itself -- a belt,
a linkage, a second gear stage. Leave at 1.0 for actuators mounted coaxially
on the joint axis. ratio_type sets the default efficiency and is one of:
direct | planetary_1stage | planetary_2stage | cycloidal | harmonic | belt | worm

ratio.note: actuator mounted coaxially on the joint, no extra reduction

_load: What the joint has to move, all referred to the JOINT output.
gravity_factor: 1 = axis horizontal so the link swings against full gravity,
0 = vertical axis so gravity never loads the joint.
gravity_phase: the joint angle at which gravity torque peaks.
link_inertia is about the joint axis and should include the link itself;
the payload's own m*r^2 is added from payload_mass and com_distance.
_profile: A repeated trapezoidal point-to-point move. This is the 'few inputs, lots of
output' path: give a stroke, a move time and a dwell, and the tool builds the
whole torque/speed/time history including inertia, gravity and the reflected
rotor inertia of the actuators actually fitted.
dwell_time is the rest between traverses and is the main knob you have over
heating -- the charts sweep it for you.
If you already have a measured torque/speed history, delete this block and
_duty_segments: Alternative to profile: an explicit [[dt, torque, speed], ...] history at the
JOINT, with the units declared alongside. Takes precedence over profile if
both are present. Include the rest periods as zero-speed segments -- and note
that a gravity-loaded joint still draws holding current at zero speed.
_POWER_SYSTEM: Bus voltage is a property of THIS robot, not of the actuator. The vendor's
rated voltage is only what they characterised the unit at. Set the voltage
your robot actually supplies here; the actuator file declares the range it
will accept, and the two are checked against each other.
Running ABOVE the vendor nominal is routine and simply extends the speed
envelope -- higher voltage buys speed, not torque and not thermal margin.
Running above their stated MAXIMUM is limited by transistor and DC-link
capacitor ratings rather than by heat, so it cannot be cleared on thermal
grounds; set accept_overvoltage true to acknowledge the risk and downgrade
that check from a failure to a warning.
Omit bus_voltage entirely to fall back to the actuator's nominal.
supply_current_limit is optional -- omit it if the supply can always deliver
more than the drive's own current rating, which is the usual case.

bus_voltage.note: state the pack you actually use, e.g. 13S lithium

_THERMAL: T_ambient is the air INSIDE your shell next to the actuator, not room
temperature. It is routinely 15-25 degC above ambient in an enclosed arm and
it moves the thermal verdict more than almost anything else.
max_surface_temp turns the computed housing temperature into a pass/fail
criterion, and is frequently the real constraint on a human-adjacent robot.
ISO 13732-1 is the relevant standard for touch limits; the threshold depends
on material and contact duration, so set it from your own safety case. Omit
it if the housing is not reachable by an operator.
mounting sets the default case-to-ambient thermal resistance and is one of:

T_ambient.note: inside the arm shell, NOT room temperature

max_surface_temp.note: housing reachable by the operator; set from your own safety case

_REQUIREMENTS: Optional hard requirements. Anything omitted is derived from the motion
above, so only set these where you have a real specification to meet: they
are combined with the computed demand using whichever is larger.
require_backdrivable adds a check that the joint can be pushed by hand,
_OPTIONAL_REQUIREMENTS: "lead": {"value": 5, "units": "mm"}   <- prismatic joints: m per output rev
